 Sunderland and Brentford meet in the round of 16 of the EFL Carabao Cup 2026/27 at the Stadium of Light this Wednesday 28 October, with kick-off scheduled for 19:45 (UK time).
 Sunderland sit bottom of the Premier League with five points from eight matches, leaving Régis Le Bris set to rotate heavily ahead of Saturday’s trip to Coventry. Brentford arrive sixth in the top flight and unbeaten on the road, having already scored eight goals across two away ties in this competition.
 With the hosts balancing domestic survival and European fixtures, this Sunderland vs. Brentford prediction points towards the visitors as strong favourites to reach the quarter-finals.

 Sunderland vs. Brentford - Head-to-head record
 Across 22 competitive meetings in all competitions, Sunderland hold 10 victories to Brentford’s seven, alongside five draws.
 Recent encounters have favoured the Bees , who have lost just one of their last eight matches against Sunderland (four wins, three draws).
 The sides met in the Premier League in September, drawing 1-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium where Enzo Le Fée cancelled out Vitaly Janelt’s second-half opener.
 At the Stadium of Light, Sunderland have won six of their 10 meetings with Brentford, including a 2-1 league victory in August 2025.
 However, with both managers rotating their squads for midweek cup action, past league meetings will have little bearing on this Wednesday’s tie .

 Sunderland - Searching for consistent form
 Régis Le Bris’ side enter Wednesday night prioritising Premier League survival, having won once in their opening eight league matches. Below is an overview of the hosts’ current form, team news, and projected starting XI:
 Recent form
 The Black Cats sit 20th in the top flight with five points. Sunday’s 0-0 draw against Leeds ended a four-match losing streak and brought their first clean sheet since August, but finishing remains an issue: Sunderland have failed to score in their last three domestic matches and have managed only three goals in their last six home games.
 In the EFL Cup, they progressed with a 1-0 third-round home win over Hull City.
 Le Bris will rest key starters ahead of Saturday’s match against Coventry. Top scorer Brian Brobbey will be held back after playing 65 minutes on his return from a hamstring injury against Leeds, allowing 20-year-old forward Timur Tutierov to start up front.
 Winger Romaine Mundle (knee) is out, and Wilson Isidor is doubtful, leaving Chemsdine Talbi, Habib Diarra, and Malick Fofana to start behind the striker.
 Midfielders Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fée will be preserved, with Jules Ahoka partnering Chris Rigg in central midfield.
 In defense, Daniel Ballard and Thomas Meunier remain sidelined with hamstring injuries, so Melker Ellborg starts in goal behind Nordi Mukiele, Luke O’Nien, Omar Alderete, and Dayann Méthalie.

 Brentford - Searching for consistent results
 Keith Andrews takes his squad to the North East sitting sixth in the Premier League, with one defeat in 10 matches across all competitions this season. Here is an examination of the visitors’ form, cup rotation, and expected starting lineup ahead of kickoff:
 Recent form
 The Bees have been tough to break down, though five draws in eight league games have slowed their progress.
 Away from home, Brentford are undefeated in all competitions this term , drawing four Premier League fixtures and winning both of their EFL Cup ties. They scored six past Birmingham City in round two and beat Reading 2-1 in round three, scoring eight goals in two away cup games.
 Andrews is without left-back Rico Henry, who faces weeks out with a hip and quad injury, while Antoni Milambo (knee), Joshua Dasilva (hamstring), and Kaye Furo (foot) remain sidelined.
 Yehor Yarmoliuk serves the second match of a three-game suspension, but Vitaly Janelt returns from a ban to anchor central midfield alongside Mamadou Sangaré .
 In attack, Callum Wilson leads the line after scoring at Reading, flanked by Fábio Carvalho, Mikkel Damsgaard, and Dango Ouattara. Goalkeeper Ellery Balcombe starts behind Michael Kayode, Kristoffer Ajer, Nathan Collins, and El Hadji Malick Diouf.

 Predictions for Sunderland vs. Brentford - Visitors to Progress
 Sunderland are resting key forward Brian Brobbey to protect him for the league, leaving an inexperienced front line that has managed three goals in its last six home fixtures. Brentford have scored in every competitive match this season, averaging 4.0 goals per game in the EFL Cup. Backing Brentford to score the opening goal is a solid primary angle.
 While Sunderland held Leeds to a goalless draw on Sunday, their second-string backline faces a severe test against Callum Wilson and Fábio Carvalho. With Sunderland managing only three goals in their last six home games, backing Under 2.5 total goals carries value if Brentford manage the game cautiously.
 Sunderland’s priority is Saturday’s league fixture at Coventry, making cup progression secondary. Brentford possess greater squad depth, remain unbeaten away from home, and have targeted this tournament under Keith Andrews. Back Brentford on the Moneyline to win within 90 minutes.
